assertion_analysis.condition: Removing native omp decoding or losing name/command propagation fails the literal bash: sleep 1200 expectation.

Reinstating the duplicate scanner makes the observed shared-owner call list empty; this failure is recorded in reuse-negative.log. The expected stream is fixture-derived but invocation is independently observed, so bypassing the owner does not move both sides together.
Removing tool_execution_start/update decoding or toolCall message-block support fails the literal bash/sleep 90 tuple for the corresponding parameter.
Dropping native omp command decoding or bounded-wait recognition returns None rather than the independent literal a 90s sleep.
Treating an argument-free update as a complete command or skipping an argument-free read start loses the literal read/empty tuple.
Ignoring the newer nonwaiting read call and reusing the old bash sleep returns a wait rather than None; the prior assertion requires a positively decoded read call.

The expected command variable is also serialized into the fixture at line 223, but it is independently constructed source content, not a result supplied by the reader; removing omp decoding or breaking carry reconstruction across 300000 characters returns None or corrupt content and fails the assertion. This is a content round-trip check, not evidence of delegation.
